lines.text: Do you know how a four digit PIN protects your phone? There are only ten thousand possible codes.
A computer could try all ten thousand in about a second, if it were allowed to.
So your phone doesn't allow it. The check happens inside a separate security chip, which counts every wrong attempt.
After a few misses, it makes you wait. A minute, then five, then an hour. Trying every code would take years.
Many phones can even erase themselves after ten wrong tries.
And your PIN is mixed with a secret key built into that chip, so the data can't be copied off and cracked somewhere else.
Orbi uses the same idea for files. A locked file needs its passcode, the server only keeps a fingerprint of it, and twelve wrong tries lock the file.
